cover.title: Cyclic sort
cover.lead: Numbers from 0 to n in about n seats: put each number in its own seat, then spot the wrong one.
cover.use_it_when: The array holds numbers from 0 to n (or 1 to n) and something is missing or repeated.
cover.why_it_matters: It finds missing and repeated numbers in place, with no extra array.
cover.promise: You'll write cyclic sort in {lines} lines.

slides.title: Numbered seats
slides.scene: Ticket 3 sits in seat 3, ticket 0 in seat 0. When everyone is seated, the seat with the wrong ticket shows who never came.

blocks.text: Seat 2 holds 5, not 2. So [[2 is the missing number]].

slides.title: Swap until home
slides.lead: Swap nums[i] into its seat. Move i on when the number is home or has no seat.

quickcheck.question: Cyclic sort on 1 2 0. Which number from 0 to 3 is missing?
quickcheck.answer: Answer: {{missing_number([1, 2, 0])}}. Every seat matches, so the missing one is n.

blog.summary: Numbers from 0 to n in an array of about n seats: put each number in its own seat.
blog.tested_inputs: hand-picked cases (one number, the missing number at either end, the LeetCode examples) and random shuffles of 0 to n with one number taken out for n up to 15, plus one shuffle of 0 to 5,000
blog.tested_against: checking every number from 0 to n
blog.tested_extra: The swaps, the skip count and the trap's crash come from running the code.

caption.first: Cyclic sort for LeetCode 268 Missing Number: seat each number at its own index, then find the wrong seat.
lines: Swap nums[i] into seat nums[i] until it's home or has no seat.
The trap: forget seat < n and the number n reads past the end.
